ky_midnight_surf.blurb: Midnight Surf is a small sport wall inside Muir Valley in the Red River Gorge. Eleven routes share a long, steeply overhanging face of sandstone, and the climbing is dynamic, with big moves between holds. The grades sit firmly at the hard end: one route at 5.11, six at 5.12 and four at 5.13, so there is nothing here for newer leaders. It is one of the valley's walls aimed at strong climbers, alongside the Sanctuary and the Solarium. Expect powerful, sustained lines rather than technical slab, and a fair amount of walking from the main lot to reach it.

ky_lower_sky_bridge_ridge.blurb: Lower Sky Bridge Ridge is a small trad buttress in the Northern Gorge of the Red River Gorge, close to the concrete bridge in the eastern part of the gorge and to Eastern Sky Bridge Ridge. About eleven routes are known, nearly all gear climbs, with one aid line. Difficulty spans from an easy line through the 5.6 to 5.9 range up to a few 5.11s and a 5.12, so there is something for most trad climbers. The wall faces south and warms up by late morning, which makes it a pleasant choice on cool days. The walk is short and trail-free, straight up the ridge from the road.

ky_3_up_rising_wall.blurb: Up Rising Wall is the farthest of the three crags at Murder Branch, near Cave Run Lake and Morehead, on a forest road well beyond the Red River Gorge's main climbing zones. It holds eleven routes, seven of them trad and four sport, on hard, colourful sandstone. Grades run from an easy 5.4 up to a 5.11, with the bulk landing between 5.9 and 5.10. It is a small wall with only a handful of lines, but several are considered high quality, so it suits a mixed-ability pair wanting somewhere quiet. The walk from the road is very short, with no real trail system.
